label: text
text: The following items of interest are extracted from thó Harbour Mutter's report for 1925:—

label: text
text: The total shipping entering and clearing at ports in the Colony during the year 1925 amounted to 370,177 vessels of 41,469,884 tons, which compared with the figures of 1924 show a decrease of 384,315 vessels and a decrease of 15,261,493 tons.

label: text
text: Of the above 41,336 vessels of 32,179,063 tons were engaged in foreign trade as compared with 57,765 vessels of 38,770,499 tons, in 1924.

label: text
text: There is a decrease in British ocean-going shipping of 1,381 ships or 26.1 per cent. and a decrease of

label: text
text: This decrease in ships and tonnage is due to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.

label: text
text: Foreign ocean-going vessels have decreased by 1,911 ships and by 2,243,124 tons or 22.3 per cent. in numbers and 13.1 per cent. in tonnage. This decrease in ships and tonnage is due to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.

label: text
text: British river steamers have decreased by 3,062 ships with a decrease in tonnage, of 1,069,546 tons or 43.0 per cent. in numbers and 16.3 per cent. in tonnage. This decrease in ships and tonnage is due to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.

label: text
text:
Foreign river steamern show a decrease of 1,052 ships with a decrease in tonnage of 387,459 tons or 45.4 per cent. in numbers and 48.1 per cent. in tonnage. This decrease in ships and tonnage is due to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.
In steamships not exceeding 60 tons employed in foreign trade there is a decrease of 2,445 ships with a decrease in tonnage - of 66,336 tons or 31.2 per cent. in numbers and 28.7 per cent. in tonnage. This decrease in launches and tonnage is due to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.

label: text
text: Junks in foreign trade show a decrease of 6,578 vessels, and a decrease of 847039 tons or 23.9 percent. in numbers and 25.6 percent. in tonnage. This decrease is due to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.

label: text
text: In local trade (i.e. between places within the waters of the Colony): there is a decrease in steam-launches of 367,826 and a decrease in tonnage of 8,571,867 tons or 54.2 per cent. in numbers and 51.5 per cent. in tonnage. This decrease in numbers and tonnage is due to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.

label: text
text: Junks in local trade show a decrease of 1,060 vessels and a decrease of 98,180 tons or 3.8 percent. in number and 7.4 percent. in tonfage. This decrease in vessels is due principally to the recent strike and the present boycott in South China.

label: text
text: Of vessels of European construction 4,776 ocean steamers, 3,085 river steamers and 2,696 steamships not exceeding 60 tons entered during the year, giving a daily average of 28.9 ships as compared with 41.2 ships in 1924 and 34.7 ships in 1923.

label: text
text: The average tonnage of individual ocean vessels entering the port has increased from 2,129.8 to 2,472.9 tons," British ships from 2,234.3 to 2,529.4 tons, foreign ships from 2,057.6 to 2,434.2 tons. The average tonnage of individual River Steamers entering during the year has remained the same at 659.8 tons," British River Steamers have increased from 891.5 to 848.4 tons and Foreign River Steamers have decreased from 310.3 to 332.9 tons.

label: text
text: The actual number of individual ocean-going vessels of European construction during the year 1925 was 1,015 of which 371 were British and 644 foreign. In 1924 the corresponding figures were 1,123, 416 British and 707 foreign. These 1,015 ships measured 3,171,253 tons. They entered 4,776 times and gave a collective tonnage of 11,810,938 tons. Thus 108 less ships entered 1,708 less times and gave a collective tonnage less by 1,999,086 tons, an average of 1,170.4 tons per entry.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tonnage

label: text
text: In 1924 there were 6,484 steamers with a tonnage of 13,800,974. In 1925 there were 4,776 steamers with a tonnage of 11,810,938 showing a decrease of 1,708 steamers and a tonnage of 1,999,036. The number of river steamers in 1924 were 4,715 with a tonnage of 3,632,438 and in 1925 there were 9,085 with a tonnage of 2,947,843 showing a decrease of 1,630 river steamers and a tonnage of 684,590. The total number of steamers and river steamers for 1924 were 11,199 with a tonnage of 17,442,412 and in 1925 7,861 with a tonnage of 14,758,738 showing a decrease of 8,388 vessels and a tonnage of 2,888,826.

label: text
text: The total revenue during the year was $878,118.83 as against $997,530.74 collected in the previous year - showing a decrease of $119,411.91 or 13.6 per cent.

Lighthouses and Signal Stations.
Gap Rock Lighthouse. During 1925 a total "number of 1,619 vessels" were signalled and reported including 315 by flash lamp, 2,618 messages, including meteorological observations for the Observatory, were sent by telegraph, and 87 by wireless, 134 messages were received by telegraph and 169 by wireless including weather reports. Telegraphic communication was interrupted for 37 hours. There were 75 hours and 25 minutes of fog, and fog signals were fired 473 times. The fortnightly reliefs were delayed; times owing to bad weather.

label: text
text: Waglan Lighthouse. During 1925, 3,335 vessels were signalled and reported, including 819 by flash lamp, 3,925 messages, including meteorological observations for the Royal Observatory were sent and 946 were received and 167 messages were sent by wireless and 149 received. Telegraphic communication was interrupted for 6 hours 25 minutes. There were 485 hours 25 minutes fog and fog signals were fired, 6,079 times. The Diaphone fog signal was sounded for 343 hours 29 minutes for fog, and 33 hours 34 minutes for testing purposes.

label: text
text: Green Island Lighthouse and Signal Station. During 1925, 1,400 vessels were signalled and reported. 12 vessels were not reported owing to telephonic communication being interrupted. 314 messages were sent and 12 were received. The number of Aga lights (including Green Island) is now 17 and have worked accurately and satisfactorily throughout the year. The Bookwith Bell was in operation from January 1 to May 31 and worked satisfactorily.
